FTMO.long:
FTMO is the largest forex and CFD funded-account provider and the sector's usual reference point. It has operated since 2015, which by the standards of this industry is a very long time, and runs a two-phase evaluation with a scaling programme that raises allocation and profit share as a trader compounds.

One structural fact separates it from most competitors. Over 2025-26 it acquired the regulated broker OANDA and re-entered the United States, so unlike the majority of funded-account providers it now sits attached to an actual regulated brokerage rather than operating purely as a simulated-product seller. That does not make the funded accounts themselves regulated instruments, but it does change the corporate substance behind them.

Its own published pass figures for the two-phase evaluation have historically sat around nine to ten percent, which is roughly in line with the sector and notable mainly for being published at all.

Where people get fooled: treating size and longevity as a verdict on the model rather than on the firm. FTMO being durable and paying reliably says nothing about whether any individual trader clears an evaluation, and the base rates apply here as everywhere. The firm's stability is a reason to worry less about counterparty risk, not a reason to expect a different outcome.
FTMO.usage: Named as the largest and longest-running forex and CFD funded-account provider.

Topstep.long:
Topstep is the longest-running of the futures funded-account providers and predates most of the current sector. Its distinguishing feature is commercial rather than technical: it charges a recurring monthly subscription rather than a one-off evaluation fee.

That inverts the cost arithmetic. Under a one-off fee, a slow evaluation costs nothing extra and a fast failure costs the whole fee. Under a subscription, the meter runs for as long as the attempt takes, so a cautious trader grinding toward a target over several months can spend more than someone who fails quickly and walks away. Neither model is inherently better, but they reward opposite behaviour, and the subscription is the one that penalises patience.

It uses an end-of-day trailing drawdown rather than an intraday one, and over 2025-26 moved onto a mandatory in-house platform and added a route for transferring earnings.

Where people get fooled: comparing a subscription price against a one-off evaluation fee as though they were the same number. The honest comparison multiplies the monthly figure by a realistic number of months, including the months spent failing, and the realistic number is usually larger than the one people assume when they sign up.
Topstep.usage: Named as the oldest futures funded-account provider and the main example of the subscription cost model.

Apex Trader Funding.long:
Apex is the highest-volume futures funded-account provider by its own reported payout figures. It is also the clearest example in the sector of a firm that rewrites its rules substantially and often.

On 1 March 2026 it replaced its rulebook wholesale, introducing a ban on holding positions overnight and caps on total payouts per account. Both changes materially alter what the product is, and both arrived after large numbers of people had already bought accounts under the previous terms. Anything written about this firm — including this entry — should be assumed to be partly out of date.

It advertises a first-attempt pass figure well above the five-to-ten percent the rest of the sector reports. That may reflect genuinely more forgiving rules, since it has historically run without a daily loss limit. It is also a self-published number from a firm selling evaluations, and no independent audit of it exists.

Where people get fooled: buying on the strength of rules that can be changed underneath them. In this sector the terms of service are the product, and a firm with a track record of rewriting them has demonstrated that the product bought today is not necessarily the one held next quarter. That is a risk worth pricing, not a detail.
Apex Trader Funding.usage: Named as the largest futures funded-account provider by self-reported payouts.

FundedNext.long:
FundedNext is one of the larger forex and CFD funded-account providers, having grown very quickly from a 2022 start. It runs several evaluation models alongside each other rather than a single flagship product.

That multiplicity is the thing worth understanding. When a firm offers a conventional two-phase evaluation, a one-phase version, an instant-funding option and various hybrids simultaneously, the marketing tends to describe the brand while the meaningful differences — the drawdown mechanics, the consistency requirements, the payout timing — sit inside each individual model. Two accounts bought from the same firm on the same day can be substantially different products.

Its reported payout totals are large and, as everywhere in this sector, self-published without independent audit.

Where people get fooled: choosing the firm and assuming the account follows. With a multi-model provider the account type is the actual decision, and the cheapest or most heavily promoted model is frequently the one with the tightest loss floor or the strictest consistency cap. The comparison that matters is between that firm's own models, not between firms.
FundedNext.usage: Named as a large multi-model forex and CFD funded-account provider.

The5ers.long:
The5ers is among the longer-established forex funded-account providers, running multi-tier programmes in which allocation grows as a trader meets successive targets rather than in a single step.

Its age is the genuinely useful fact about it. This is a sector in which most firms are only a few years old, several have closed without warning, and at least one large operator was the subject of a major regulatory action. Having operated across more than one market cycle, and through the periods when competitors failed, is one of very few signals available to someone assessing counterparty risk from the outside.

That is a weak signal rather than a strong one. Longevity is evidence a firm has not yet failed, which is not the same as evidence it will not.

Where people get fooled: reading a scaling ladder as a plan rather than as a possibility. Multi-tier programmes are presented as a path from a small allocation to a large one, and the path exists, but the proportion of entrants who traverse it is governed by the same base rates that apply to every evaluation. Each tier is another filter, and the compounding of those filters is rarely shown alongside the ladder.
The5ers.usage: Named as one of the longer-running forex funded-account providers, using tiered scaling.

Prop firm landscape.long:
Beyond the handful of widely known names there are many funded-account providers, and the field changes constantly. On the futures side the recurring names include Take Profit Trader, MyFundedFutures, Tradeify, Bulenox, TickTickTrader and Earn2Trade. On the forex and CFD side they include Funding Pips, FXIFY, The Funded Trader and Alpha Capital Group.

New entrants appear continually because the barrier is low: the model requires a platform licence, a payment processor and a rulebook, not a balance sheet or a registration. Some of these firms are durable and pay reliably. Others have closed abruptly, changed terms retroactively, or been bought and rebranded.

Placing an unfamiliar firm is therefore a matter of a few checks rather than of reputation. How long has it operated, and through what conditions? Is the funded account simulated, and who is the counterparty? Are payout claims independently verifiable or self-reported? What does the agreement say about changing its own terms?

Where people get fooled: taking comparison sites and ranking tables at face value. Almost all of them earn a commission per referral, which means the ordering reflects payout rates to affiliates at least as much as quality, and a firm's absence from a list often means it declined to run an affiliate programme rather than that it is worse.
Prop firm landscape.usage: Used for the wider field of funded-account providers beyond the best-known names.
